segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְפִסְחוֹ, אוֹ זָכָר בֶּן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים — יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב, וְיִמָּכֵר, וְיִפְּלוּ דָּמָיו לִנְדָבָה לִשְׁלָמִים.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one who separates a female» animal «for his Paschal lamb» although the Torah requires a male, «or a male that is in its second year» although a Paschal lamb must be an animal that is in its first year, the animal «is left to graze until it» develops a blemish and «becomes unfit, and it is» then «sold and its money is used for free-will offerings» or «peace-offerings.»

segments.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ פִּסְחוֹ וּמֵת, לֹא יְבִיאֶנּוּ בְּנוֹ אַחֲרָיו לְשֵׁם פֶּסַח אֶלָּא לְשֵׁם שְׁלָמִים.
segments.en: With regard to «one who separates his Paschal lamb and» then «dies, his son» may «not bring it after him for the purpose of a Paschal lamb» because it may no longer be used for that purpose after its owner has died. «Rather,» it is brought «for the purpose of a peace-offering.»

moves.summary: unfit animal separated as Paschal lamb grazes; proceeds to free-will offerings
owner died: son brings it as a peace-offering

positions.claim: a female or two-year-old male separated for a Paschal lamb grazes until blemished, and its money goes to free-will peace-offerings
if the owner died, the son brings it as a peace-offering, not a Paschal lamb
